description.value: The study examined resting-state habenula functional connectivity in autistic and neurotypical individuals, including diagnostic group differences, age-related developmental variability, functional decoding, and associations with autism-related phenotypic measures.

design.value: This was a multisite, cross-sectional resting-state functional MRI study using participants selected from the ABIDE I and II datasets. Participant-level habenula-to-whole-brain correlation maps were compared between ASD and NT groups and modeled as a function of age, sex, scanning site, and phenotypic measures.

name.value: Behavior Rating Inventory of Executive Function (BRIEF) Global Executive Composite Score (GEC) T-score

description.value: The BRIEF GEC T-score measured executive function by compiling scores from three composite indexes testing behavior regulation, emotional recognition, and cognitive regulation.

The DLS domain measured adaptive behavior encompassing everyday tasks necessary for independent living, including personal care, household responsibilities, and community activities such as maintaining hygiene, preparing meals, and managing money and time.

task_description.value: Resting-state functional MRI data were used to calculate whole-brain functional connectivity maps from left and right habenula regions of interest.

description.value: Resting-state functional MRI data were acquired across 24 scanning sites using 3T MRI scanners. Full acquisition parameters and site-specific protocols were available from the ABIDE website.

For all participants, a T1-weighted structural image was collected and used for registration to Montreal Neurological Institute space. Structural MRI data were acquired across the 24 scanning sites using 3T MRI scanners.
Data were preprocessed using fMRIPrep 23.1.3 with manual and automated quality control, followed by denoising of the remaining participants using AFNI's 3dTproject.

steps.value: Anatomical images were spatially normalized to MNI152 space.
Participants with a fail rating from any independent ABIDE I rater were manually excluded.
MRIQC was used to inspect, flag, and remove participants, sessions, or runs with framewise displacement greater than 0.35 mm or fewer than 100 usable time points after motion censoring.
AFNI's 3dTproject performed nuisance time-series regression from each voxel within the dataset.

model_settings.value: For each participant, averaged left and right habenula ROI time series were entered into a general linear model to generate whole-brain correlation maps. Correlation maps were Fisher r-to-z transformed.

Z-transformed participant-level correlation maps were entered into group-level regression models with diagnosis (ASD, NT) as a categorical factor and age as a continuous factor, controlling for sex and scanning site.

Among participants aged 5–21 years, z-transformed participant-level correlation maps were analyzed using a linear effects model to probe age-by-group interactions, controlling for sex and scanning site.

Z-scored beta coefficients extracted from clusters showing atypical habenula connectivity were entered into linear regression models as a function of Social Motivation, Social Communication, Executive Function, or Daily Living Skills, testing phenotypic main effects among ASD participants and interactions between ASD and NT groups while controlling for age, sex, and scanning site.

roi_definition.value: Bilateral habenula ROIs were manually defined on the MNI’s 152-subject averaged T1 template brain (i.e., ICBM152), following the procedure for manual habenula delineation outlined by Lawson et al.
